source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company maintained zero long-term debt and a net cash position in FY25 (shareholder funds ~Rs 8,104 crore, negligible borrowings; FY25 operating cash flow Rs 1,947 crore vs Rs 1,118 crore in FY24).

inr_exposure.evidence: Company imports several Diageo global brands (Johnnie Walker, Baileys, Lagavulin, Talisker) creating USD-denominated cost exposure; key domestic raw materials (ENA, molasses, glass) saw glass bottle cost inflation of ~12-15% and ongoing ENA inflation in FY25, partly offset by pricing/productivity (gross margin +115bps to 44.5%). No explicit export revenue % or formal hedging policy text found in available sources; business is overwhelmingly India-domestic (IMFL/P&A focus).

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme applicable to alcoholic beverages sector; none found in sources.

rural.evidence: VECV's new Eicher Pro truck series described as gaining traction 'in both urban and rural markets'; no revenue % disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: VECV bus segment (35% market share in FY25) driven substantially by government/STU contracts; management cited 'reduced infrastructure activity' as a demand headwind for the CV business in Q2 FY25, indicating linkage between truck demand and infra/govt capex cycles.

inr_exposure.evidence: Royal Enfield international/export revenue was Rs 2,546 crore in FY25 (~13.5% of RE's Rs 18,870 crore standalone revenue), up 38% YoY; RE holds ~9% market share in Europe, ~8% in Americas, ~9% in Asia-Pacific; new CKD (completely knocked down) assembly plants opened in Thailand and Brazil to grow export markets (No.1 in UK, No.2 Argentina, No.3 Brazil). VECV exports are comparatively small and volatile (e.g., -38.8% in one recent month).

pli_scheme.evidence: Royal Enfield has applied for Auto-PLI incentives tied to localisation of EV powertrain, electronics and battery-pack components ahead of its first electric motorcycle; third-party analyst estimates suggest potential incentive receipts of Rs 200-600 crore over the scheme period, contingent on localization and incremental sales targets (not yet confirmed as accrued benefit in financials).

china_plus_one.evidence: CFO's Review, Annual Report 2024-25: 'As global supply chains continue to diversify, our strong alignment with India's industrial growth becomes increasingly evident.' Also: 'more than 70% of our revenue comes from markets outside India, with North America alone contributing 40%.' No explicit 'China+1' framing tied directly to order wins; company itself has manufacturing plants in China (Hangzhou) and is investing in domestic rare-earth magnet production to reduce reliance on Chinese magnet imports (an import-substitution story rather than a customer-diversification-to-India story).

govt_capex.evidence: Post the Escorts Kubota railway business acquisition, Sona Comstar supplies brakes, couplers and suspension systems with 'a long-term partnership with Indian Railways' and is 'market leader in its product segments' (a government-capex-linked customer); segment revenue % not separately disclosed for FY25.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Consolidated financial statements, Note on interest rate risk: 'Variable rate borrowings Rs 134.63 million; Fixed rate borrowings Nil; Total borrowings Rs 134.63 million' as at 31 March 2025 (down from Rs 2,330.58 million variable-rate borrowings a year earlier) - company is effectively near debt-free with what little debt remains being fully floating-rate.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials are special steel alloy bars and forgings, not crude/oil derivatives; cost of materials consumed was Rs 13,878.6 million on standalone revenue of Rs 30,928.5 million (~45%) but this is a steel/metal cost, not a crude-oil-linked input.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Board-approved hedging policy primarily using forward contracts
inr_exposure.evidence: Directors' Report / MD&A: 'Your Company operates internationally, and a large portion of the business is transacted in international currencies primarily in US$ and EUR... exposed to foreign exchange risk through our sales and services in the USA, Europe, China and other countries... The Company carries out currency hedging based upon a Board approved hedging policy which primarily employs forward contracts.' BRSR disclosure: 'The contribution of exports to total turnover of the entity is 57%.'

pli_scheme.evidence: CFO's Review, Annual Report 2024-25: 'We benefited from income accrual from the Auto PLI scheme, for which we had eight products approved.'

china_plus_one.evidence: 'As global pharmaceutical companies are diversifying their API supply chains away from China, Divi's Labs seems to be a good play to take advantage of this shift with its strong product mix, robust financials and aggressive capex outlay... a status further solidified by the China Plus One procurement strategy.' Company also cites 'diversified sourcing strategies' and reduced China dependence in its own raw-material procurement (solvent recovery, backward integration), and custom synthesis (53% of product mix) growth tied to innovator customers seeking non-China supply.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company maintained a debt-free balance sheet with strong free cash flows in FY25.

crude_exposure.evidence: Cost of materials consumed steady at approximately 40% of revenue; solvents (petrochemical/crude-derivative inputs) are a major cost component, mitigated via in-house solvent recovery systems and backward integration to reduce input costs and single-source supplier risk.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Natural hedging via high export revenue share offsetting import costs; no large forward-hedging program disclosed
inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue by geography: Europe Rs 5,192 cr (56.5%), North America Rs 1,488 cr (16.2%), India Rs 1,105 cr (12.0%), Asia Rs 1,044 cr (11.4%), RoW Rs 367 cr (4.0%) - 88% of sales revenue derived from exports. Company reported forex gains of ~Rs 48 crore in FY25 vs Rs 30 crore in FY24, consistent with natural hedging from export-heavy revenue mix.

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's has announced PLI-supported capacity expansions in API segments where Chinese pricing had previously made domestic investment unviable, under India's PLI scheme for KSMs/Drug Intermediates/APIs (Rs 6,940 crore outlay, FY2022-23 to FY2028-29).

china_plus_one.evidence: Press coverage (Manufacturing Digital, BusinessToday) notes ABB has invested over US$230M over the past decade to strengthen India's position as a global manufacturing hub, with new Hyderabad/Nashik investment for circuit breakers and expansion into rail/metro exports; framed as export-diversification momentum rather than an explicit 'China+1' claim with revenue attribution in the AR itself (AR text not directly accessible).

govt_capex.evidence: Order backlog of Rs 9,995 crore as of Sep-2024 (+25% YoY) attributed to 'government-led capex revival' with large orders from infrastructure, power transmission/grid, railways, metals, data centers and renewables (per earnings-call/press coverage); no specific % of revenue from government/PSU customers disclosed in sources found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: ABB India is a low-debt/cash-generative subsidiary; no specific floating-rate borrowing breakdown found in accessible sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company described as exporting to over 30 countries; no quantified USD revenue % or hedging policy detail found.

rural.evidence: Company case-study coverage ('Nestlé India Bets on Rural Push to Sustain Growth') and prior press estimates put rural sales at roughly 20-25% of domestic revenue (dated 2020-21 estimates, not a confirmed FY24-25 AR figure); company continues to emphasize rural distribution expansion as a stated growth strategy in recent commentary.

crude_exposure.evidence: Press coverage notes 'rising raw material costs and crude-linked packaging expenses putting pressure on margins,' though milk, green coffee and wheat are cited as the largest raw material cost drivers rather than crude itself; no % breakdown of crude-linked inputs found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company sources 'more than 97% of its materials locally,' implying limited direct import/FX exposure on raw materials, though it is 'not fully insulated from inflation' per press coverage; no hedging policy text found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Nestlé India received Government of India approval (Dec 2021) under the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI), specifically for the processed fruits & vegetables category; incentive payouts run through FY2026-27. No revenue % attributable to the scheme disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Emcure has a vertically integrated in-house API business and a large international formulations business (~53.7% of FY25 revenue, +20.5% YoY). Broader industry/press coverage ties India's API-focused PLI scheme (for KSMs/APIs) to reducing China dependence, and frames 'China+1' as a general Western-pharma sourcing goal, but no Emcure-specific AR statement explicitly attributing its revenue/order growth to China+1 diversification was found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Finance costs fell 25.9% YoY in FY25 and current liabilities declined from ~Rs 32B to ~Rs 27B per equitymaster's AR analysis, suggesting deleveraging, but no specific floating-rate-debt % was disclosed in sources found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Natural hedging — offsets foreign-currency payables (trade obligations, loans) against foreign-currency receivables, supplemented by financial instruments for residual risk (per CARE Ratings press release commentary); no formal hedging ratio disclosed.
inr_exposure.evidence: International revenue of ~Rs 4,236 crore out of total Rs 7,896 crore in FY25 (~53.7%), growing faster (20.5%) than domestic (16.4%).

rural.evidence: Tier-III and beyond cities contribute approximately 3% of Dr Lal PathLabs' revenues, growing at a 17% four-year CAGR versus ~14% overall revenue CAGR over the same period; company commentary (Q4/FY25 results coverage) emphasizes expansion into Tier-III/Tier-IV towns via new labs (~280 labs, ~5,700 collection centers nationally) as a growth strategy, alongside strengthening rural/secondary healthcare access.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Total debt of roughly ₹1.6B against a debt-to-equity ratio of ~7%, with cash and short-term investments (~₹11.6B) exceeding total debt and finance costs down ~24% YoY in FY25 — indicates minimal balance-sheet leverage and low interest-rate sensitivity overall, though no specific floating-vs-fixed borrowing split was disclosed in sources found.

rural.evidence: Analyst/earnings commentary on FY25: 'growth in Emerging India continued to be higher than in Urban Markets'; company has focused on distribution expansion into rural and smaller towns (no % disclosed in sources reviewed)

crude_exposure.evidence: Third-party analyst reports give inconsistent estimates of VAM (a crude-oil derivative) as 30-60% of raw material cost (e.g. 'VAM forms 35-40% of overall raw material costs' in one broker note, 'roughly 50% of raw materials are crude oil derivatives' in another); no single AR-sourced figure could be confirmed, so left null per no-invention rule

rate_sensitive.evidence: Titan sources gold via Gold Metal Loans (GML) from banks, gold exchange at outlets, and spot buying; company described as 'fully hedged at all times' on gold procurement — a commodity/lease-rate exposure rather than a disclosed floating-rate debt %; no interest-rate debt breakdown found

crude_exposure.evidence: Not applicable — Titan's core inputs are gold, diamonds and components, not crude-oil derivatives

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Reported as 'fully hedged at all times' on gold procurement (bullion sourced via banks' Gold Metal Loan scheme, gold exchange, and spot buying); a 1% rise in gold price historically translates to ~2% EBIT increase due to pricing pass-through and hedging structure
inr_exposure.evidence: Rating agency commentary: 'effective hedging policy' cited as a credit strength; Titan management notes gold prices 'expected to remain elevated and volatile'

govt_capex.evidence: Medanta participates in government health schemes (Ayushman Bharat, CGHS) with longer receivable cycles (CGHS ~200+ days, Ayushman Bharat ~100+ days), but this is government health-insurance scheme revenue, not government capex-linked revenue; no % of revenue from these schemes was found

inr_exposure.evidence: Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report (BRSR) disclosure: 'contribution of deemed export of services was 5.19% of total turnover in FY2024-25 compared to 4.94%' [prior year] — reflects international-patient revenue treated as deemed exports; Q4FY25 international patient revenue also cited at ~6% of quarterly revenue

china_plus_one.evidence: Company sells IMFL to 100+ countries but no China+1/supply-chain-diversification framing was found; exports described simply as ~10% of core IMFL revenue

rate_sensitive.evidence: Total debt ~Rs 737 crore at FY2024-end (debt:equity ~0.3x), largely from capex on Rampur dual-feed distillery and Sitapur greenfield project (~Rs 891-950 crore cumulative capex since FY22); company targets debt-free status by FY26/FY27; no specific floating-vs-fixed rate breakdown disclosed in sources reviewed

crude_exposure.evidence: Not applicable — core raw materials are ENA (extra neutral alcohol), grain and molasses (agri-based), not crude-oil derivatives; company has invested in backward integration (dual-feed molasses/grain plant at Rampur) to secure agri-input supply, not crude

inr_exposure.evidence: 'Exports make up about a tenth of revenue in Radico Khaitan's core Indian-made foreign liquor business, which sells to more than 100 countries' (press coverage); no formal hedging policy disclosure found

china_plus_one.evidence: Industry commentary notes anti-dumping duty on Chinese tiles and a 'China plus one' shift has favoured Indian tile exporters generally (mainly the export-oriented Morbi cluster), but Kajaria itself is domestic-focused with exports only ~1.08% of FY25 turnover, so no company-specific China+1 revenue attribution.

rural.evidence: Management commentary cites tier II/III city demand and distribution network expansion (900 dealers in FY14 to ~1,500 currently) as a growth driver amid a residential real-estate upturn in FY25, but no explicit rural revenue % disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Commentary notes a 'positive rub-off effect' on tile demand from government's infrastructure push and real estate upturn, but this is indirect consumer/housing demand, not direct government capex order revenue; no % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company carries low debt (D/E ~6.3%, interest coverage ~23x, FY25 interest paid ~Rs 20 crore); floating vs fixed split not disclosed in sources found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Power and fuel (natural gas/propane, kiln energy) costs were nearly 20% of Kajaria's FY25 revenue and estimated at 35-40% of production cost; average gas cost ~INR 37-41/SCM through FY24-FY25, a key margin-sensitive energy input tied to global gas/crude-linked pricing.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (~1.08% of FY25 turnover) fell due to Red Sea disruption and freight costs; company is overwhelmingly domestic-revenue (INR) with minimal USD exposure.

govt_capex.evidence: Business is entirely driven by government and public-sector customers — Ministry of Defence, DRDO, HAL, BEL, ECIL and BrahMos Aerospace are the main counterparts; order book ~INR 2,062 crore (including negotiated orders), FY26 order inflows ~INR 1,121 crore (+216% YoY).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company was zero-debt as on March 31, 2024 per company disclosure, implying negligible floating-rate liability exposure, though not explicitly quantified.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports were ~16% of revenue in FY23 (Rs 72 crore) but fell to ~5% in 9M FY24; export order book ~INR 53 crore as company engages Europe/international customers and expects export revenue to grow going forward.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmation found of Data Patterns as a PLI (electronics manufacturing) scheme beneficiary; its business model is direct defence/government procurement rather than the consumer-electronics PLI scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company is described as built around a 'China-plus-one' strategy with minimal dependence on Chinese raw materials; CEO/Founder Ajay Bhardwaj: 'We're now the second source for many products made in China, and the first choice for new ones,' with management framing itself as a China-alternative CDMO driving order/revenue growth (cost arbitrage cited in IPO commentary).

inr_exposure.evidence: High export orientation — exports to over 44 countries with a large share of revenue from Europe and the US; exports contributed ~85% of revenue from operations per company BRSR-type disclosure (FY25-26 period, closely applicable to FY24-25 run-rate). Top 5 clients account for ~70.9% of FY25 revenue, concentrating both client and currency risk.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmation found of Anthem Biosciences on the approved-applicant list for the pharma/bulk-drug PLI scheme.

rate_sensitive.evidence: IHCL is effectively net-debt-free apart from lease liabilities, with unencumbered cash and liquid investments of over Rs 2,400 crore and undrawn credit lines of over Rs 300 crore (as of Sep 2024); long-term debt fell from Rs 14bn (FY22) to Rs 3bn (FY23), reducing floating-rate exposure materially, though no explicit floating-rate % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: International hotels/portfolio contributed roughly 19% of IHCL's consolidated operating revenue (comparative disclosure around FY25/Q1 FY26), with international portfolio revenue growing further to ~Rs 1,725 crore in FY26; domestic same-store hotels drove ~12% YoY RevPAR growth, outperforming industry benchmarks by 73%.

china_plus_one.evidence: Bosch aims to double exports from India by 2030 (Guruprasad Mudlapur interview, Business Standard, Jul 2025); company cites geopolitical uncertainty affecting supply chains and a 'local for local' resilience commitment; Powertrain Solutions FY25 growth of 5.8% partly attributed to tractor segment and rising export sales.

pli_scheme.evidence: Bosch secured PLI approval (March 15, 2022) under the Component Champion Incentive Scheme of the Auto PLI Scheme, one of 67 approved companies; revenue/quantum not disclosed in sources found.

govt_capex.evidence: MD&A/press commentary attributes demand tailwind to government-driven infrastructure expansion (railways, roads, gas pipelines, urban housing); domestic steel demand growth estimated at 7-8% annually driven by infra/urbanization spend. No exact revenue % disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Shyam Metalics Flat Products selected under the PLI Scheme for Specialty Steel, described as market leader/most competitive bidder among steel players in that scheme; revenue contribution not disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Indian Air Force alone historically >70% of turnover (CAG audit); remaining domestic customers are Navy, Army, Coast Guard, MoD/DRDO — i.e. virtually all non-export revenue is Indian government/defense-linked. Exports are only ~1% of total revenue, with HAL targeting to raise export share to 25% (current export contracts ~Rs 300 cr in 9M FY25). FY25 revenue from operations Rs 30,980.95 crore (consolidated), up ~2% YoY.
